```{r}
#| label: setup
REPO <- "https://github.com/fhoces/opa-prop40/blob/main/"
for (f in list.files("../R", pattern = "[.]R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
root <- comparison_root()
link <- function(path, text = path) sprintf('<a href="%s%s"><code>%s</code></a>', REPO, path, text)
# Money in running text: a dollar sign in markdown starts a formula, so escape it.
usd <- function(x, d = 1, s = FALSE) gsub("$", "\\$", money(x, d, s), fixed = TRUE)
# "(a)" in a raw HTML table cell reads as a list marker to pandoc, and a bare dollar sign
# can start a formula, so both are written as entities.
ent <- function(x) gsub("\\(([a-z])\\)", "&#40;\\1)", gsub("$", "&#36;", x, fixed = TRUE))
show <- function(df) {
  df[] <- lapply(df, function(x) if (is.character(x)) ent(x) else x)
  knitr::kable(df, format = "html", escape = FALSE, row.names = FALSE,
               table.attr = 'class="table table-sm"')
}
scroll <- function(x) cat('\n<div class="table-scroll">\n\n', x, "\n\n</div>\n\n", sep = "")
first_comment <- function(f) {
  l <- readLines(f, warn = FALSE, n = 12)
  l <- sub("^(#+|\"\"\")\\s?", "", l[grepl("^(#|\"\"\")", l)])
  l <- l[nzchar(trimws(l))]
  if (length(l)) l[1] else ""
}
# The test suite, run while this page renders, so the counts below are this commit's.
res <- as.data.frame(testthat::test_dir(file.path(root, "comparison", "tests", "testthat"),
                                        reporter = "silent", stop_on_failure = FALSE))
```

::: {.report-intro}
![](assets/opa/opa-materials-wordmark.png){.opa-figure}

This page is a guide to the **Open Materials** layer (the repository folder) of the
comparison, the reconciliation of the [BSZ analysis](../../bsz-analysis/site/) and the
[JR analysis](../../rjkdc-analysis/site/), each in its latest version (BSZ, August 2026;
Jaros and Rauh, September 2026). It says what to run, what the tests check, what
each file is, and what the checks found. Everything lives in one repository,
[fhoces/opa-prop40](https://github.com/fhoces/opa-prop40), under `comparison/`. The tables on
this page are built from the files when the page is rendered.
:::

## Rebuild everything

```sh
git clone https://github.com/fhoces/opa-prop40 && cd opa-prop40
pip install scipy                         # the Python twin's one dependency
Rscript comparison/run.R                  # export/r, export/py, index.html, site/explorer/, assets/comparison-data.js
Rscript comparison/tests/testthat.R       # the test suite
python3 comparison/py/bridge.py           # the Python twin alone, writes export/py/
cd comparison/site && quarto render repro.qmd && quarto render materials.qmd
```

The comparison needs nothing downloaded. It reads each analysis's *export contract*: the two
files `export/r/inputs.csv` and `export/r/outputs.csv` that each analysis's own pipeline writes
for others to read. Both are committed, so the comparison rebuilds without either analysis's
sources. It also reads the values transcribed from the PDFs in `comparison/data/`. Set
`OPA_PROP40_ROOT` if the scripts cannot find the repository root, and `PYTHON` to choose the
interpreter `run.R` calls for the Python twin, `py/bridge.py` (the same computation written a
second time in Python and checked against the R result).

## Tests

```{r}
#| results: asis
by_file <- aggregate(cbind(blocks = 1, passed = nb - failed - skipped, failed, skipped) ~ file,
                     data = transform(res, skipped = as.integer(skipped)), FUN = sum)
by_file$file <- vapply(by_file$file, function(f) link(paste0("comparison/tests/testthat/", f), f), "")
scroll(show(rbind(by_file, data.frame(file = "<b>total</b>", blocks = sum(by_file$blocks),
                                      passed = sum(by_file$passed), failed = sum(by_file$failed),
                                      skipped = sum(by_file$skipped)))))
```

Run while this page was rendered: **`r sum(res$nb - res$failed - res$skipped)` expectations
passed, `r sum(res$failed)` failed**, in `r nrow(res)` test blocks. The files check:

- `test-endpoints.R`: each end of the bridge against the number its authors print (BSZ
  Table 5 row 1, the NBER mean NPV; NBER is the National Bureau of Economic Research, which
  circulates working papers), plus the earlier figures the code still checks: the
  headline of GGSS (the Galle, Gamage, Saez and Shanske expert report of July 2026, by some of
  the experts who drafted the initiative, GGSS p.1), behind the BSZ analysis, and the March
  2026 version of the JR analysis. The bridge itself ends at the September 2026 version.
- `test-shapley.R`: the Shapley steps sum exactly to the gap in every setting, and match a
  brute-force average over orders (a Shapley value: a step's effect averaged over every order
  the inputs could be switched in, so the steps add up to the gap).
- `test-parity.R`: the R exports are current, and the Python twin's agree with them to 1e-9.
- `test-sources.R`: every transcribed input has a label, a source and a page.
- `test-site.R`: the overview page and the explorer are exactly the generator's output, have
  no unfilled token or em-dash, show the key numbers and the two main estimates, the explorer's
  data file carries the same two values, the switchboard (the common function's value for every
  on/off mix of the `r nrow(bridge_steps())` inputs) equals the two ends at its all-off and all-on
  settings in every horizon setting, the explorer's slider panels start and end at the two
  analyses' estimates, `site/explorer/model.js` (run with node) returns the R value on every mix
  in `slider_sample.csv` to 1e-9, the explorer shows no gross revenue number, and every
  relative link resolves.

GitHub Actions rebuilds the exports in R and Python on a clean runner and runs the suite on
every push that touches `comparison/` or either analysis's export contract
(`.github/workflows/comparison-ci.yml`). It does not render the Quarto pages.

## Scripts

```{r}
#| results: asis
role <- c(
  "R/contract.R" = "reads the two export contracts and the document inputs, and nothing else",
  "R/model.R" = "score_common(), the one estimating function; the dial path; exact Shapley over all orders; one sequential order; the JR Monte Carlo's expectation",
  "R/build.R" = "every number the page shows, written to export/r/*.csv",
  "R/site.R" = "renders the overview page (index.html), the explorer (site/explorer/index.html) and their data file from site/index.template.html and site/explorer.template.html",
  "py/bridge.py" = "the Python twin of contract.R, model.R and build.R; writes export/py/*.csv",
  "run.R" = "builds all three: the R exports, the Python exports and the two pages",
  "tools/digitize_hoopes_fig2.py" = "reads Hoopes (2026) Figure 2 off the chart into data/hoopes-fig2.csv",
  "site/explorer/model.js" = "score_common() and the slider rule ported to JavaScript; the explorer's panels run it in the browser (written by hand, checked against slider_sample.csv)",
  "site/repro.qmd" = "the reproduction report",
  "site/slides/slides.Rmd" = "the slide deck: what is in the report and where the main differences come from (xaringan; every number read from export/r/)",
  "site/materials.qmd" = "this page")
fs <- names(role)
scroll(show(data.frame(
  file = vapply(fs, function(f) link(paste0("comparison/", f), f), ""),
  lines = vapply(fs, function(f) length(readLines(file.path(root, "comparison", f), warn = FALSE)), 1L),
  `what it does` = unname(role), check.names = FALSE)))
```

## Data files the site publishes

```{r}
#| results: asis
n_args <- nrow(read.csv(file.path(root, "comparison", "export", "r", "inputs.csv")))
desc <- c(
  "inputs.csv" = sprintf("the disputed inputs: one row per argument of the common function (%d), grouped by bridge step, both analyses' values and sources", n_args),
  "bridge.csv" = "every step's Shapley value and one-order value, for each output and horizon setting",
  "ends.csv" = "the two ends of every bridge (BSZ, Jaros and Rauh NBER) for each output and horizon setting, and the model difference at the JR end (zero by construction, kept as a check)",
  "endpoints.csv" = "each end against the number its authors print",
  "anchors.csv" = "the two revenue numbers of the JR analysis's September 2026 version, as candidates for where the steps end on output (a) (an anchor: the published number an end of the bridge is checked against)",
  "loss.csv" = "every annual income tax loss on one scale, with present values",
  "hoopes.csv" = "Hoopes (2026) Figure 2 beside the bridge read in his order",
  "meta.csv" = "intermediate values the page quotes (annuity factors, the BSZ net terms)",
  "switchboard.csv" = "the common function's value for every mix of switches (bit i of mask = disputed input i at the JR value), for each output and horizon setting",
  "slider_sample.csv" = "300 slider mixes per explorer panel (positions 0 to 4 per input, 0 = the panel's own analysis) and the panel's value, the sample the tests run model.js on")
dfs <- names(desc)
rd <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(root, "comparison", "export", "r", f))
scroll(show(data.frame(
  file = vapply(dfs, function(f) link(paste0("comparison/export/r/", f), f), ""),
  rows = vapply(dfs, function(f) nrow(rd(f)), 1L),
  columns = vapply(dfs, function(f) ncol(rd(f)), 1L),
  contents = unname(desc))))
own_a <- subset(rd("ends.csv"), horizon_setting == "own" & output == "a")
```

In `inputs.csv`, the `supporting_*` columns hold the BSZ analysis's values and sources, and the
`rauh_*` columns the JR analysis's.

`loss.csv`'s last column, `net_at_nber_revenue_perpetuity`, nets each loss in perpetuity
against the JR analysis's expected revenue (`r usd(own_a$rauh_own)`, in `ends.csv` and
`anchors.csv`).

`comparison/export/py/` holds the same files from the Python twin (without `inputs.csv`).
The explorer reads `assets/comparison-data.js`, written by `R/site.R`
from these files. Its two slider panels read the two input vectors from the same data file and
compute each panel's estimate in the browser with `site/explorer/model.js`, which follows
`slider_inputs()` in `R/model.R`: positions 1 to 3 are evenly spaced between the two values, and
the horizon steps through 5, 10, 20 and 50 years and a perpetuity. The inputs the comparison transcribes itself are in
`r link("comparison/data/document-inputs.csv")`
(`r nrow(read.csv(file.path(root, "comparison", "data", "document-inputs.csv")))` rows, each
with an origin label, a source and a page) and
`r link("comparison/data/hoopes-fig2.csv")` (Hoopes's Figure 2, read off the chart). None is
edited by hand except these two transcriptions.

## Sources

The comparison reads no third-party file at run time. Each analysis's sources are listed on its
own materials page ([BSZ](../../bsz-analysis/site/materials.html),
[JR](../../rjkdc-analysis/site/materials.html)). The comparison alone uses three documents.
Two of them, Hoopes (2026) and the LAO's ballot analysis, are recorded in this manifest with
where to get them and their SHA-256:

```{r}
#| results: asis
ds <- read.csv(file.path(root, "comparison", "DATA-SOURCES.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
scroll(show(data.frame(
  file = sprintf("<code>%s</code>", sub("^original-materials/", "", ds$file)),
  provider = ds$provider,
  obtained = paste(ds$obtained_via, ds$date_obtained),
  `SHA-256 (first 12)` = sprintf("<code>%s</code>", substr(ds$sha256, 1, 12)),
  terms = ds$terms, check.names = FALSE)))
```

Full rows: `r link("comparison/DATA-SOURCES.csv")`. Neither PDF is redistributed. The third is
Walczak (California Tax Foundation, 22 April 2026), whose row is in the JR manifest
(`r link("rjkdc-analysis/DATA-SOURCES.csv")`).

The GGSS expert report (20 July 2026), which the bridge cites for the non-citizen residents,
the avoidance allowance and the litigation step, and the GGSS response to Rauh (17 March 2026),
which `DISPUTES.md` cites for the March 2026 disputes, are listed in the BSZ analysis's manifest,
`r link("bsz-analysis/DATA-SOURCES.csv")`, with their URLs on Saez's Berkeley page.

## What the checks found

```{r}
ex <- read_exports(file.path(root, "comparison", "export", "r"))
k <- read_contracts(root)
ep <- ex$endpoints; own <- ex$ends[ex$ends$horizon_setting == "own", ]
ea <- own[own$output == "a", ]; eb <- own[own$output == "b", ]
oo <- k$rjkdc$outputs
```

The full crosswalk of disputed inputs, with every page reference checked against the PDFs, is
`r link("comparison/DISPUTES.md")`. The checks behind the bridge found:

- **The September 2026 ceiling has three values.** The script draws revenue up to the literal
  72; the README prints 72.06; the person-level file sums to
  `r formatC(pick(oo, "nber_ceiling", "value"), format = "f", digits = 2)` (the JR analysis's
  mismatch 4). The comparison uses the script's 72, so the common function returns the
  authors' own expected revenue exactly and the bridge has no model-difference step.
- **The litigation weight has no multiplier in the code.** The README applies q = 0.50 to the
  recognized base for the point estimate and lists a uniform draw of revenue between 0 (struck
  down) and the ceiling for the simulation. The script has no separate q; its draw's mean is
  the same half (mismatch 5). The comparison reads that mean as the weight `q`.
- **The printed NPV is one run, not the expectation.** The exact expectation of the NBER
  Monte Carlo is `r usd(eb$rauh_own, 2)` against a printed
  `r usd(ep$printed_value[ep$endpoint_id == "rauh_nber_npv"])`. The bridge's JR end is that
  expectation, with the authors' random rate replaced by the one rate worth the same,
  `r rate_txt(ex$meta$value[ex$meta$key == "r_jr"])` ([the report](repro.html#the-discount-rate)). The JR pipeline reproduces
  the seeded run as `r usd(ep$contract_value[ep$endpoint_id == "rauh_nber_npv"], 3)`. The
  comparison's pages use the exact expectation as the JR main estimate.
- **Both analyses' discount factors are right.** One reading magnifies the loss by a factor
  67 (1/1.5%), BSZ say 33 (1/3%). The first is the rate the JR text anchors its range of r &minus; g on, the second the mean
  rate of its Monte Carlo (`DISPUTES.md`, row 2). Averaged over the draw the perpetuity factor is
  ln(3)/0.03 = `r formatC(ex$meta$value[ex$meta$key == "A_inf_jr_draw"], format = "f", digits = 1)`, the value of one rate of `r rate_txt(ex$meta$value[ex$meta$key == "r_jr"])`, the JR end of the comparison's rate dial (row 10).
- **Two March disputes are closed in the BSZ analysis by August**: Larry Ellison's exclusion
  and the non-US-citizen residents (rows 7 and 8).
- **One Hoopes bar could not be traced.** His confirmed-departures bar matches no number in
  the March 2026 version of the JR analysis (see the [report's Hoopes section](repro.html#the-hoopes-comparison)).
